statement: Structural validity is not semantic approval. This receipt records what the listed structural checks observed against one candidate at one moment. It does not certify that the figures on the board are correct, that the underlying delivery data is fit for a decision, or that this candidate is approved for release. Business meaning and release authority remain with named humans.

corpus_amendments.reason: Expectation was over-stated: it assumed all ten rail links are exposed without interaction. Corrected to the candidate's fold-based rail design after direct observation. No assertion was weakened; the test now performs the interaction a user would.

Expectation of zero serious/critical axe violations was not met by the candidate. Rather than deleting the check or marking it passed, the two observed violations are recorded as named open defects and baselined, so the gate now detects NEW serious violations. The open defects are carried into every receipt.

Both defects were fixed in the candidate (s4u-methodology PR #70, 4161ec2) and verified absent by an axe probe on the live page; a baseline that no longer describes the candidate would let a regression hide behind it.

New cases authored before the candidate change was built: the owner found that the redesign had dropped the DORA mapping the original board carried. Run against the unchanged live candidate first, where they are expected to fail.

Pinned counts raised for a planned candidate change, before it was built: one new fold on Delivery today (12 to 13) and three not-assessed state cells in its mapping table (198 to 201). No assertion was weakened.
